title: European Council grants EU candidate status to Ukraine and Moldova
body:
On 23 June 2022 the European Council adopted conclusions on the membership applications of Ukraine, the Republic of Moldova and Georgia. The conclusions were published by the European Commission on 24 June. The Council recognised the European perspective of Ukraine and Moldova and decided to grant both countries candidate status.

The Commission was asked to report on whether the conditions set out in its opinions on the two applications were met, as part of its regular enlargement package. The Council said it would decide on next steps once those conditions were fully met. For Georgia, the Council recognised its European perspective and said it was ready to grant candidate status once the priorities in the Commission's opinion were addressed. Georgia therefore did not yet receive candidate status.

On Ukraine, the Council reaffirmed its support, condemned Russian attacks on civilians and called for a further increase in military support. It noted the adoption of the sixth EU sanctions package, said the Commission would propose exceptional macro-financial assistance of up to 9 billion euros for 2022, and called for the Black Sea ports, including Odesa, to be unblocked. Progress for each country was to depend on its own merits in meeting the Copenhagen criteria.
